## Claims
- [source-backed] Schur functions are homogeneous by partition weight; \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) inherits this grading, with multiplication truncated to partitions in \((n-r)^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269]
- [source-backed] \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution, hence preserves Littlewood–Richardson multiplication under conjugation. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]
- [computed] For the non-self-conjugate pair
  \[
  [222,4^5]\subset\Lambda/I_{5,4},\qquad [33,5^4]\subset\Lambda/I_{4,5},
  \]
  complete \(A_+J\)-relation matrices and quotient Smith data in weights \(6,\ldots,20\) agree: free ranks are
  \[
  (1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0),
  \]
  in weights \(6,\ldots,20\), and all torsion-factor lists are empty. [artifact 5b6e59b74af1b386568e8d3014cdef276ec80f89225cf5ba2367c73fa3b0a993]
- [proved] Conditional on accepted quotient conjugation and ideal correspondence, partition conjugation induces an integral graded isomorphism
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\;\cong\;J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee},
  \]
  preserving degreewise integral torsion subgroups and free ranks.

## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\),
\[
A=\Lambda/I_{r,q},\qquad A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r},
\qquad
\Omega(\bar s_\lambda)=\bar s_{\lambda'}.
\]
Accepted quotient conjugation gives \(\Omega:A\!\xrightarrow{\sim}\!A^\vee\), and accepted ideal correspondence gives
\(\Omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\). Since \(|\lambda'|=|\lambda|\),
\[
\Omega(A_d)=A^\vee_d,\qquad
\Omega(A_+)=A^\vee_+,
\]
where \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\) and \(A^\vee_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A^\vee_d\). Therefore
\[
\Omega(A_+J_v)=A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}.
\]
Restricting and passing to quotients yields the displayed integral graded isomorphism. In each weight \(d\), it is an isomorphism of finitely generated abelian groups, so it preserves element orders, torsion subgroups, invariant factors, and free \(\mathbb Z\)-rank. The \(a=0\) singleton-interval boundary is included, since the argument uses no positivity of \(a\).

The artifact ID is its stable digest. This finite computation is a bounded verification only.

## Gaps
The universal corollary is conditional on the accepted quotient-conjugation and ideal-correspondence premises. The finite computation does not prove those premises or any parent theorem.
